hypothesis: Determine whether CPU-only mode in the same compiled helper actually executes OpenCL work or only eagerly probes/initializes vendor context.

facts.fact: Backend registration/probe creates a shared cl_context during eager device enumeration.
ggml_cl_init initializes the per-device compute backend separately.
Backend init calls ggml_cl_init and increments backend refcount.
OpenCL supports_op may lazily initialize compute state if queried.
CPU mode selects no accelerator devices, n_gpu_layers0, op_offloadfalse and offload_kqvfalse.

conclusion: CPU-only in the OpenCL-enabled helper includes vendor driver/context discovery; CPU model/graphs are explicitly CPU resident. Device-detected log is not proof of GPU computation. No idle GPU power/energy effect measured; pure CPU-only build sensitivity can be a later control if any marginal OpenCL win emerges.
